To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heterodyne XPCS method can be used to study the dynamics of the carbon-black skeleton of elastomers and the flow of the elastomer.

the method of coherent X-ray photon correlation spectrometry can be used to study slow relaxation processes of materials, and that it can separate the contribution of the sample flow to the observed speckle changes.

we have demonstrated a new technique, X-ray photon correlation spectrometry (XPCS), which is capable of measuring the dynamics of materials with a time resolution in the nanosecond regime and a spatial resolution of 10 µms, and that we have used this technique to measure the dynamics of a carbon-black-filled elastomer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics of materials by means of X-ray photon correlation techniques.
the study of the dynamics of soft matter using X-ray photon correlation spectrometry.
the use of coherent X-rays to study the dynamics of complex systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the case of the carbon-black elastomers, heterodyne correlation spectroscopy allows the observation of slow fluctuations and flow, whereas homodyne measurements allow the determination of the correlation time of the fast fluctuations.
, in the absence of flow, the heterodyned signal is the same as the homodyned signal, but the homodyned speckle signal is not the same as the heterodyned one.
heterodyning is not a necessity in X-ray photon correlation experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heterodyne technique allows the study of fluctuations of small particles, but also of the flow of large particles and of the slow relaxation of elastomers.
heterodyne measurements provide more information on the relaxation process than homodyne measurements.
the heterodyne technique is a very powerful tool for the study of slow relaxation processes, which are not accessible by the conventional homodyne method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heterodyne XPCS technique is well suited for the study of very weakly fluctuating samples.
, in the presence of a long-term flow of the sample, the heterodyning method can be used to separate the fluctuations from the long-term flow of a material.
heterodyne XPCS is a very promising technique to study slow relaxation processes in soft matter.
